name: AI Engineering & Multi-Agent Platform
description: Specialist agents behind a model gateway, with tool authorization, human approval and tracing.

capabilities.name: Agent orchestration
capabilities.summary: Teams: a lead agent delegates sub-tasks to its members (one level deep, budgeted). Each run has a full trace.

capabilities.name: Model gateway
capabilities.summary: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, any OpenAI-compatible server (Azure OpenAI, Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter, vLLM) and AWS Bedrock Converse. Keys come from a host env var or are stored encrypted. Adapters are tested against stub servers; run Test on each provider to check your real key.

capabilities.name: Model selection
capabilities.summary: Each agent picks its provider and model. Teams can mix providers.

capabilities.name: Prompt versioning
capabilities.summary: Not built yet. System prompts are edited in place and not versioned.

capabilities.name: Agent memory boundaries
capabilities.summary: Not built yet. Every run starts with no memory of earlier runs.

capabilities.name: Tool registry
capabilities.summary: Built-in read-only tools: current_time, list_modules, cache_search (AWS data cache).

capabilities.name: Tool authorization
capabilities.summary: An agent can use a tool only if it lists it and the caller has the tool's minimum role.

capabilities.name: Human approval
capabilities.summary: Not built yet. There are no write tools, so agents cannot change infrastructure. Write tools will need approval through M03.

capabilities.name: Hallucination controls
capabilities.summary: Not built yet. Answers are not checked against sources.

capabilities.name: Prompt injection protection
capabilities.summary: Tool output is wrapped as data and the system prompt says not to follow it. This reduces risk but does not guarantee it.

capabilities.name: Data leakage prevention
capabilities.summary: Obvious secrets (AWS keys, password/token values, private keys) are redacted from tool output before the model sees it. Prompts still go to the chosen provider, so pick providers your data policy allows.

capabilities.name: Execution tracing
capabilities.summary: Each run stores every model call, tool call, delegation, token count and duration.

capabilities.name: Cost monitoring
capabilities.summary: Token counts are recorded for every run. Cost in currency is shown only when you enter the provider's price per million tokens.

design.guardrail: Agents call the same APIs as people. They cannot bypass authorization, policy checks or production approvals.
